AMIDOWN is a supplier of premium-quality Polish goose down and natural goose and duck down-and-feather blends. We specialise in the selection, processing and supply of natural fillings that meet the requirements of premium manufacturers and comply with international standards and global quality expectations. Our fillings are used in bedding, home textiles and upholstered furniture. The foundation of AMIDOWN is the knowledge and many years of experience of our founder, Dawid Mielczarski, who has developed his own approach and quality standards for working with natural down and feathers. Every stage of the process—from selecting the raw material to its final preparation—is subject to strict quality control. We work according to internationally recognised standards, precise technical specifications and consistent production processes that ensure long-term reliability for our business partners. LOOKING FOR A RELIABLE DOWN & FEATHER SUPPLIER? Contact us to discuss your material specifications and explore cooperation opportunities. CONTACT US. B2B ENQUIRY. KNOWLEDGE. EXPERTISE. FOUNDATION. Our collection of natural duvets and pillows is the fulfilment of Dawid’s long-held vision. His passion for natural fillings and years of industry experience became the foundation of the AMIDOWN brand. At the heart of every duvet lies one of nature’s finest insulators —premium Polish Kołuda goose down, renowned worldwide for its exceptional thermal performance. Our products are created with deep respect for nature and ethical sourcing practices, supported by internationally recognised certifications including RDS, IDFB, IDFL and OEKO-TEX®. These certifications give you confidence that you are choosing a natural, safe and responsibly produced product that meets the highest international standards. PASSION. Every AMIDOWN duvet and pillow tells our story—one built on respect for nature, craftsmanship and a genuine passion for creating exceptional products. For more than eighteen years, our CEO, Dawid, has dedicated his career to understanding every aspect of natural down and feathers. His expertise spans every type of filling, its unique properties and its full potential. I bring a feminine perspective and understated elegance to the brand. Every collection I design reflects my belief that true beauty comes from nature itself. Together, in the heart of Greater Poland, we create products made by skilled hands, rooted in Polish craftsmanship and shaped by experience—bringing you the comfort, authenticity and tranquillity that only natural materials can provide. Milena Mielczarska, Co-founder. QUALITY & EXPERIENCE. At AMIDOWN, I believe true quality is built on responsibility, passion and experience. That is why every stage of creating our duvets and pillows takes place under our own supervision—from the very beginning. We source feathers from trusted local farms, supporting Polish agriculture. We process them in our own manufacturing facility using proprietary technology and machinery. Every batch is tested in our in-house quality laboratory. Our experienced specialists oversee every step of production, ensuring the standards that define AMIDOWN. POLISH GOOSE DOWN. Anyone searching for the world’s finest goose down eventually turns their attention to Poland. For decades, Poland has been recognised as one of the world’s leading sources of premium goose down and feathers. This reputation is the result of a unique combination of factors that cannot easily be replicated elsewhere. A key element is the exceptional genetics of the Polish Koluda goose, developed and protected by the National Research Institute of Animal Production in Koluda Wielka. Equally important are rigorous farming standards, carefully balanced natural feed, controlled bird development and a strong commitment to animal welfare. Poland’s distinct four-season climate also plays an essential role, allowing the birds’ plumage to develop naturally and reach its full insulating potential. Together, these factors make Polish goose down one of the most valued natural fillings in the world. LEARN MORE. Furniture filling and furniture cushion sewing are an essential part of producing upholstered furniture, ensuring a suitable, stable construction and a high level of comfort in use. Furniture inserts affect the comfort, durability and stability of the furniture. Explore our offer. Contact us. Offer Overview. The comfort of upholstered furniture depends to a large extent on the quality of the furniture cushions used and the filling chosen. At ELJOT we specialize in producing a range of components used by furniture manufacturers, providing comprehensive sewing services. We also prepare furniture cushions to the customer’s individual requirements. We handle orders end to end for large production plants and smaller companies looking for a proven, trusted partner for sewing and preparing cushions for upholstered furniture. What furniture cushions do we make? We make a range of furniture cushions used in lounge, garden and commercial furniture. We produce: seat cushions,. back cushions,. decorative cushions,. corner cushions,. cushions for sofas and couches,. cushions for armchairs,. cushions for garden furniture. All projects can be matched to the specific dimensions, shapes and performance parameters set by the furniture manufacturer. Individually selected fillings. Depending on the purpose of the cushion and the comfort of use expected, different filling materials are used. In production we use, among others: feathers and down,. flame-retardant feathers,. polyurethane foam,. foam chips,. silicone fiber balls,. shredded foam granules. Fabrics we use for sewing: polypropylene spunbond nonwoven fabric (wigofil),. inlet (inner casing) fabric,. upholstery calico,. other materials used in the furniture industry. The choice of filling affects the resilience, softness, durability and appearance of the finished product. With our experience we help choose the solution that best suits the particular piece of furniture. Blending different types of filling. We offer the option of blending different fillings. We have a specialist mixer that lets us combine different filling materials (e.g. feathers and down, flame-retardant feathers, polyurethane foam, foam chips, silicone fiber balls) in the right proportions. This gives the best performance parameters for the cushions and lets us match their properties to the furniture manufacturer’s individual requirements. Blends of different fillings are an increasingly sought-after service in the furniture industry, because they make it possible to produce a product that is comfortable, suitably durable and attractive in appearance. Why choose ELJOT Firma? With us you can count on a complete service covering sewing, preparation and filling of furniture cushions. We have the right technical facilities and experience, which lets us handle individual projects as well as larger production series. By working with ELJOT Firma you gain: an individual approach to every project,. the ability to produce cushions in different shapes and sizes,. a wide choice of filling materials,. the ability to create filling blends,. on-time order fulfilment,. support at every stage of production. If you are looking for a proven partner for furniture cushion production and the preparation of high-quality fillings, get in touch. We will gladly prepare a solution tailored to your company’s needs and the specifics of the furniture you make. Warehousing and shipping. As part of our services, we offer logistics support for your business. We provide secure storage of goods in modern facilities, as well as efficient, on-time shipping. FAQ: Furniture filling production. Which furniture cushions are most commonly used in upholstered furniture? Upholstered furniture most often uses seat cushions, back cushions and decorative cushions. Which filling should I choose for furniture cushions? The choice of filling depends on the purpose of the cushion and the comfort of use expected. Furniture cushion production often uses feathers and down, polyurethane foams, foam chips or silicone fiber balls. Can different types of furniture filling be combined? Yes. Blending different filling materials (feathers with down) is becoming increasingly popular. It gives the softness, resilience and durability of furniture cushions that suit the specific application. Feather processing in Poland – Past and present - Federacja Eksporterów Polskiego Puchu i Pierza. EN. PL. Feather processing in Poland. Past and present. Feathers and down have been used in Poland for centuries for a variety of purposes – decorative, writing, for military plumes and many others. The cold climate fostered the use of feathers in comforters and pillows. As early as in the 17th century, Jan Chryzostom Pasek described in his chronicles that comforters at the royal court in Warsaw were filled with feathers. Sources from the eighteenth to nineteenth centuries mention the collection of valuable feathers for bedding in the Polish countryside, the first primitive feather-cleaning devices and craftsmen specializing in featherbed making. There is an old important tradition associated with the Polish countryside, which is called “tearing of feathers”. It literally involves separating a soft and light vane from a hard shaft of feather, so that the latter would not poke through the shell of the featherbed or pillow. Since this activity was laborious and time-consuming, the women living in a village would meet in one of the houses on winter evenings and together they would tear feathers telling each other stories and tales. Once the work was done, they would continue the same work at one of their neighbors’ house. Nota bene, traces of this tradition can be found even today, by the occasion of recycling old used feather material. Feather processing in Poland developed later than in Western Europe. During the interwar period, feathers were processed and cleaned using primitive manual methods. Significant amounts of feathers were exported to the West as unprocessed raw material. Only after World War II did people begin to invest in the mechanization of feather factories by equipping them with sorting machines, washing lines, tuggers and other equipment. During the communist period sources of feather raw material were highly fragmented and consisted of numerous small and medium-sized poultry slaughterhouses and countless small-scale farms. The latter collected feathers both from moult-harvesting and from plucking birds pos-mortem. Small traders nick-named “feathermen” used to collect the feathers from farmers and villagers and then delivered the material to wholesalers and feather processors. The last 3 decades after the fall of communism have been a period of dynamic changes in the feather industry in Poland. Many feather processing machines, such as sorting machines, complete washing lines, mixing units, dedusters, and others, both second-hand and brand new constructions, have been put into operation. Plants have been modernized, production efficiency has been increased, and the in-house quality control laboratories have been developed and well trained in feather and down quality testing. A significant amount of Polish feather raw material is now processed in Poland to be offered as ready-to-fill blends of fully washed down and feathers, reaching as high as 1000 mm turbidity. Two types of feather materials dominate Polish market: 1) from the White Koluda® goose and 2) from the Polish white pekin duck. Feathers of landfowl are no longer in use. Annual production volume of Polish white goose plumage remains relatively stable, disturbed only by occasional attacks of avian influenza. In contrast, the amount of raw plumage collected annually from Polish pekin duck has increased more than 10 times in the last 15 years. Polish manufacturers offer excellent white goose feathers and down obtained from birds raised in pure, non-industrialized regions of Poland, such as Wielkopolska, Kujawy, Pomerania, Masuria, Podlasie. Thanks to excellent vertical integration of reproduction, hatching, contract breeding and slaughtering of waterfowl, as well as compact distribution chain and local processing of original Polish feathers and down, Poland offers full traceability of origin of the material and guarantees compliance with international standards for animal welfare. Some of Polish feather processors as well as independent sewing factories are successively expanding their production of high-quality textile products. The last decade in particular has seen a renaissance, so to speak, of Polish textile production, including the manufacture of quilts, pillows, jackets, coats, sleeping bags and sports outfits. These products are not only being exported, but are also becoming more and more popular in the domestic market. As the Polish society’s prosperity increases, so does the group of consumers who value comfortable and durable down products, especially those filled with Polish white down and feathers. Polish feather and down processors and bedding manufacturers associated in our Federation are responsible and reliable business partners. Members of the association have great experience, production and commercial competence, and in-depth knowledge of the market with its limitations and opportunities.
